project_type: Next.js 14 App Router, TypeScript, Supabase, Tailwind CSS
build_system: Next.js 14 via npm; next.config.mjs uses MDX, image optimization, and serverComponentsExternalPackages. IMPORTANT: typescript.ignoreBuildErrors is true in next.config.mjs, so `next build` does NOT catch TS errors. Always use `npm run typecheck` (tsc --noEmit) to check TypeScript.
test_framework: vitest (npm run test) — no tests exist for the files being changed
verification_instructions: 1. Run `npm run typecheck` from the workspace root. Expect 0 errors after FEAT-001 and FEAT-002. 2. Run `npm run build` to confirm the build completes without critical errors.
snapshot_or_generated_files: tsconfig.tsbuildinfo (auto-generated by tsc) — do not commit this
environment_constraints: Windows PowerShell. Never run `next dev` or restart the dev server. Do not push to git. TypeScript errors are ignored during `next build` — only `npm run typecheck` reveals them.
contribution_requirements: Maintain existing NurseFiti designs, brand themes, colors, and features. Do not change route logic, component APIs, routing, or authentication logic. No new npm dependencies.
key_patterns: Supabase client is typed via `Database` interface in `lib/types/database.types.ts`. Missing table definitions cause `.from('table')` to return `never`, making all operations on that table emit TS errors. The `Database.public.Tables` object must include every table the admin routes touch. Dynamic imports use `next/dynamic` with `{ ssr: false }` for client-only components.
directory_structure: app/ — Next.js App Router pages; app/(admin)/ — admin panel; app/(student)/ — student dashboard; app/api/ — API routes; lib/types/ — TypeScript types including database.types.ts; lib/supabase/ — Supabase client helpers; supabase/migrations/ — SQL migration files (ground truth for schema); components/ — React components; middleware.ts — auth middleware
